   compute the median query ID length.
2. If median length > 6, build an ASCIIBarChart (horizontal) instead of
   ASCIIQueryHistogram (vertical). ASCIIBarChart already supports labels
   up to 30 chars and has its own truncation logic.
3. ASCIIBarChart uses BarData(label, value, ...) instead of HistogramBar.
   Map the query data into the appropriate dataclass.
4. For high query counts (>40), consider showing only the top/bottom N
   queries in horizontal mode since vertical space is limited.

Key files:
  - benchbox/core/visualization/post_run_summary.py (chart selection logic)
  - benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/bar_chart.py (ASCIIBarChart, BarData)
  - benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/histogram.py (ASCIIQueryHistogram - read only)
description:
The post-run query latency histogram uses vertical bars (ASCIIQueryHistogram)
which puts query IDs on the x-axis. For benchmarks with short numeric IDs
(TPC-H: Q1-Q22, TPC-DS: Q1-Q99) this works well. But for Primitives
benchmarks and others with long descriptive query names (e.g.,
"Qaggregation_groupby_large", "Qshuffle_inner_join_one_to_many_string"),
the labels get truncated to 2-3 characters ("Qa", "Qo", "Qsh"), making the
chart unreadable.

A horizontal bar chart (ASCIIBarChart already exists in bar_chart.py) would
put query names on the y-axis with up to 30 characters of label space,
making long names legible. The post-run summary should automatically choose
the appropriate chart type based on query name length.

Decision heuristic: if the median query ID length exceeds a threshold
(e.g., 6 characters), use horizontal bars. Otherwise use vertical histogram.

Affected benchmarks (long query names):
  - read_primitives (124 queries, names like "aggregation_groupby_large")
  - transaction_primitives
  - metadata_primitives
  - joinorder (names like "1a", "2b" - short, so vertical is fine)
  - h2odb (names like "groupby_q1" - borderline)

Unaffected benchmarks (short numeric IDs):
  - tpch (Q1-Q22), tpcds (Q1-Q99), ssb (Q1-Q13), clickbench (Q1-Q43)
